_comment: SAT-SA execution-gap rule configuration.
An execution gap is a CONTRADICTION between what evidence says was
expected and what the same evidence says actually happened.
expected control  ->  observed evidence  ->  contradiction
-> potential execution gap
This file is the ONLY place a supervisory expectation is expressed. The
detector contains no per-rule code: it reads these declarations and
evaluates them against canonical concepts. A rule is data, not logic.
MISSING EVIDENCE IS NOT AN EXECUTION GAP
If any concept in required_evidence is absent or empty for a record, the
rule evaluates to NOT_EVALUABLE and emits nothing. Absence of escalation
evidence is reported by the capability layer (evidence availability) and
the negative-space layer, never here. A gap requires proof that the
expected step was NOT done, which requires an explicit contradicting
value -- never a missing one.
WHY ONLY ONE RULE IS ENABLED
Of the 28 concepts in mappings.json, only SECURITY_SEVERITY and
ESCALATION_STATUS form an expectation/contradiction pair that submitted
alert evidence can actually prove. Every other candidate needs a
canonical status field, an SLA, or a concept that does not exist. Those
are declared under 'unavailable_rules' with the specific missing
evidence, so the gap is recorded rather than papered over with a proxy
or an invented threshold.
No numeric threshold appears in this file. A rule may only compare
explicitly submitted categorical values.
Canonical form for submitted values: trimmed, upper-cased, with
spaces, hyphens and dots folded to underscores. So 'not escalated',
'NOT-ESCALATED' and 'not_escalated' all normalise to NOT_ESCALATED.
Matching is exact against the configured vocabulary -- a value that
is not listed does not match, so an unrecognised value yields
NOT_EVALUABLE rather than a speculative finding.
The explicit submitted tokens a rule may match on, per concept.
mappings.json defines no allowed_values for any concept, so the
supervisory vocabulary is declared here instead of being guessed at
detection time. Aliases are deliberately conservative: only tokens
that unambiguously mean the same thing are listed. A token that could
also mean 'not applicable' is NOT listed, because reading it as
'not escalated' would manufacture a finding.
Deliberately narrow. NOT_ESCALATED is the only token that proves
escalation was considered and declined. Tokens such as NONE,
N/A, PENDING or blank are absent on purpose: they mean the
submission did not state an outcome, which is missing evidence
rather than a contradicted expectation.

rules.name: Critical alert explicitly not escalated
description: A supervisory expectation that an alert whose submitted severity
is CRITICAL must reach ESCALATED. This rule fires only when the
same record explicitly states both facts and they contradict each
explanation_template: Alert evidence records an explicit severity of {SECURITY_SEVERITY}
together with an explicit escalation status of {ESCALATION_STATUS}.
The supervisory expectation is that a critical alert is escalated,
so the two submitted values contradict each other.
rationale: Both concepts exist in mappings.json, both resolve from ordinary
alert submissions, and both carry an unambiguous submitted value.
The contradiction is provable from the record alone.

unavailable_rules.name: Investigation explicitly not performed
missing_evidence: No INVESTIGATION_STATUS concept exists in mappings.json.
investigation_context has no status/ performed field in the canonical schema.
The only investigation concept, INVESTIGATION_EVIDENCE, maps to
investigation_context.notes, which is free text and cannot assert
that investigation did not happen.
investigation_context.root_cause_identified and
investigation_context.remediation_identified are canonical fields
but have no mapping concept, so no source column can reach them.
why_not_implemented: Investigating 'investigation did not occur' from absent notes would
convert missing evidence into an execution gap, which this layer
must never do. Absent notes is reported as evidence availability
by the capability layer, which is the correct owner of that fact.
would_require: A canonical investigation status field plus a mapping concept, so
that a submission can state an explicit NOT_PERFORMED value.

unavailable_rules.name: Alert resolution breached the applicable SLA
missing_evidence: EVENT_TIMESTAMP and RESOLUTION_TIME both exist as concepts.
No SLA expectation exists anywhere in the repository: no
configured threshold, no severity-to-response-time table, and no
allowed_values for either concept.
response_context.acknowledgement_time is a canonical field with no
mapping concept.
why_not_implemented: Comparing a resolution time against a threshold this project
invented would be an arbitrary rule, and a defensible one cannot
be written without a supervisory authority's SLA. Any number
chosen here would encode the tool's opinion as a control failure.
would_require: A configured SLA expectation, ideally severity-banded, supplied by
the supervisory authority rather than assumed by the tool.

unavailable_rules.name: Closed alert without identified remediation
missing_evidence: investigation_context.remediation_identified is a canonical field
with no concept in mappings.json, so it is undiscoverable from any
source column.
why_not_implemented: A boolean remediation flag with no mapping concept cannot be
resolved, and a rule reading an unresolvable field would silently
evaluate as absent -- converting a wiring gap into a silent pass.
would_require: A mapping concept for the remediation field.

unavailable_rules.name: Critical asset not monitored
missing_evidence: asset_context.criticality and monitoring_context.telemetry_available
are canonical fields with no concepts in mappings.json.
The capability layer already reports both as undiscoverable.
why_not_implemented: This is an evidence-availability fact, not a contradiction
between two observed values. It belongs to the capability layer.
would_require: Mapping concepts for asset criticality and monitoring telemetry.
